evidence_records.Full citation: Zhao, Zhilong, and Yindi Liu. 2025. Automated Quality Assessment for LLM-Based Complex Qualitative Coding: A Confidence-Diversity Framework. arXiv:2508.20462v2.
evidence_records.Title: Automated Quality Assessment for LLM-Based Complex Qualitative Coding: A Confidence-Diversity Framework
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v2 dated 30 September 2025; explicitly builds on the authors' accessible-task preprint arXiv:2508.02029
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: direct methodological companion to Zhao and Liu's accessible-task confidence–diversity study (arXiv:2508.02029); distinct datasets and analyses, not an independent replication
evidence_records.Research objective: Test whether model confidence and inter-model entropy predict accuracy on complex long-text, domain-expertise classification tasks, whether their weights transfer across domains, and whether risk triage reduces verification.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: complex qualitative coding across legal, political and medical domains
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Five LLMs independently perform three pre-labelled supervised classification benchmarks; confidence and vote entropy are correlated with benchmark correctness, optimized into a weighted score, transferred among domains, and used in a simulated three-tier verification policy.
evidence_records.Domain: legal outcome prediction; hyperpartisan-news detection; medical-specialty classification
evidence_records.Dataset name: 2017 Supreme Court term benchmark; SemEval-2019 Task 4 hyperpartisan news; MTSamples
evidence_records.Number of documents: 390 Supreme Court cases; 645 articles; 1,000 medical transcripts (2,035 total)
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 2,035 long documents; one prediction from each of five models per case
evidence_records.Document length: legal cases average 8,000+ words; news articles 1,200+; medical transcripts 800+
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: public legal/news data and de-identified clinical transcriptions
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-4o-mini; Gemini-2.0-flash; DeepSeek Chat v3; Llama-4-Maverick; Claude-3.5-Haiku
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: task-specific zero/few-context classification prompts plus a risk-framed self-assessment from 0.50–0.99; exact prompts are in the replication package
evidence_records.Agent roles: models classify and report risk; ensemble entropy and confidence form a quality score; a simulated triage policy assigns verification tiers
evidence_records.Human role: no study-specific qualitative coders or adjudicators; benchmark labels act as ground truth and the proposed human role is verification of sampled cases
evidence_records.Generated outputs: class predictions, risk/confidence values, entropy, optimized weights, quality tiers
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: case-level model outputs and benchmark labels are retained in the replication data; no interpretive quotation trail is evaluated
evidence_records.Baselines: confidence-only, entropy-only, equal weighting, domain-optimized and global weights; cross-domain weight transfer
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: one prediction per model/case; 1,000 bootstrap resamples; model sampling seed not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: accuracy, Pearson correlation, bootstrap confidence intervals, Bonferroni-adjusted p-values, effect sizes and verification-effort simulations
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: none; triage verification is simulated rather than conducted
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: not applicable; benchmark correctness is the reference
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: Pearson correlations, 1,000-resample bootstrap intervals, Bonferroni correction, weight optimization, effect sizes and cross-domain transfer comparisons
evidence_records.Principal results: Entropy correlated negatively with correctness in all domains (r=-.179 to -.273); confidence correlated positively in political and medical tasks after correction. Optimized combinations improved 6.6–113.7% over confidence alone, and all transferred weights reportedly improved the confidence-only baseline. Mean simulated verification reduction was 44.6%.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: 44.6% mean simulated manual-verification reduction; five-model ensemble estimated at 3–5 times a single model's compute cost
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: secondary analysis of public/de-identified benchmarks; authors state no new ethics approval was required
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Harvard Dataverse draft replication package DOI 10.7910/DVN/GM8T8Q with datasets, code, optimization and triage scripts
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: classification rather than interpretive thematic/narrative analysis; 3–5× ensemble cost; dependence on models/prompts; long-tail cases; only three domains
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: The paper calls fixed benchmark prediction 'qualitative coding'; its quality signal is validated against known labels despite motivating deployment without ground truth. Weight optimization and triage appear evaluated on the same three datasets, and '100% transfer success' means improvement over a weak confidence-only baseline, not preservation of qualitative validity.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Extends arXiv:2508.02029 from ten accessible interview categories to three complex pre-labelled benchmarks using the same confidence–diversity concept.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strengthens uncertainty/triage as a candidate component, but lowers its ranking unless tested prospectively on held-out, interpretive coding with independent humans and verified error costs.

evidence_records.Full citation: Hairston, JaMor, Ritvik Ranjan, Sahithi Lakamana, Anthony Spadaro, Selen Bozkurt, Jeanmarie Perrone, and Abeed Sarker. 2025. Automating Inductive Thematic Analyses of Health Content Using Large Language Models: A Proof-of-Concept Study Using Social Media Data. JAMIA Open 8(5): ooaf102. https://doi.org/10.1093/jamiaopen/ooaf102.
evidence_records.Title: Automating inductive thematic analyses of health content using large language models: a proof-of-concept study using social media data
evidence_records.Authors: JaMor Hairston; Ritvik Ranjan; Sahithi Lakamana; Anthony Spadaro; Selen Bozkurt; Jeanmarie Perrone; Abeed Sarker
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; publisher/PMC full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: automated xylazine Reddit coding; expert themes originate in Spadaro et al. 2025 (JMIR Dermatology, DOI 10.2196/70329), so this is a dependent computational validation rather than an independent inductive analysis
evidence_records.Research objective: Evaluate low-shot LLM strategies for reproducing expert xylazine themes in temporally separated Reddit datasets.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Domain experts first derive twelve themes from 15 posts in prior work; prompts are iteratively tuned on DS1, then five LLMs perform one binary classifier per fixed theme, with two configurations evaluated on a temporal DS2 expert-coded sample and the best applied to 686 unlabeled posts.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: hybrid: human induction followed by deductive fixed-theme classification
evidence_records.Domain: public-health and substance-use discourse on Reddit
evidence_records.Dataset name: xylazine Reddit DS1, DS2 and DS2F
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: public posts at collection; coded texts available by data-use agreement/request
evidence_records.Number of documents: DS1 286; DS2 validation 236; DS2F 686, drawn from larger keyword collections of 5,376 and 13,928 posts
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 522 expert-coded posts plus 686 final unlabeled posts; 12 themes
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: public but sensitive substance-use and wound discussions
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: zero-, one- and two-shot prompts; each theme decomposed into a separate binary task; prompt phrasing and exemplars iteratively optimized on DS1; prompts in supplement
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: no parameter fine-tuning; prompt optimization and in-context examples
evidence_records.Agent roles: model assigns each fixed theme independently to each post
evidence_records.Human role: medical-toxicology authors induce/consolidate themes, manually annotate DS1 and DS2, tune prompts, and serve as reference
evidence_records.Generated outputs: twelve binary theme labels and theme-prevalence distributions
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: post-level labels; prompt supplement; original/coded posts restricted to request/data-use agreement
evidence_records.Baselines: expert labels; five models; zero/one/two-shot configurations; temporally later validation set
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: paper says models showed low variability across runs but does not state a reproducible run count or seed
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, 95% confidence intervals and theme-prevalence comparisons
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: expert-coded DS1 development set and temporally disjoint DS2 validation subset
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: medical-toxicology-trained authors/domain experts; exact number assigning each post and adjudication procedure not stated
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: per-theme and mean precision/recall/F1/accuracy with confidence intervals and rank comparisons
evidence_records.Principal results: On DS2, GPT-4o two-shot reached accuracy .909, precision .760, recall .663 and F1 .708; DeepSeek-V3 reached .895/.702/.642/.671. High accuracy coexisted with moderate precision/recall under class imbalance; fixed thematic distributions were similar for prevalent themes.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: API use is described as potentially costly and local open models as reducing security/cost concerns; no measured time or cost
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Emory IRB STUDY00002458; public Reddit data; coded text shared only under data-use agreement
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: prompts and supporting details in online supplement; posts recollectable through the described API; coded text by request
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: fully unsupervised induction remains difficult; moderate precision/recall; keyword filtering may omit indirect discussion
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Despite the title, model evaluation is deductive classification of expert-derived themes. The 15 DS1 posts used both to originate themes and iteratively tune prompts create development leakage, and no inter-rater reliability or annotator allocation is reported.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Computational follow-on using the code frame created in Spadaro et al. 2025 on xylazine-associated wounds.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strong evidence for temporal held-out testing and task decomposition; also a central claimed-versus-operationalized example and a warning against reporting accuracy alone on rare themes.

evidence_records.Full citation: Sankaranarayanan, Sreecharan, Conrad Borchers, Sebastian Simon, Elham Tajik, Amine Hatun Ataş, Berkan Celik, Francesco Balzan, and Bahar Shahrokhian. 2025. Automating Thematic Analysis with Multi-Agent LLM Systems. OSF Preprints. https://doi.org/10.35542/osf.io/kq8zh_v1.
evidence_records.Title: Automating Thematic Analysis with Multi-Agent LLM Systems
evidence_records.Authors: Sreecharan Sankaranarayanan; Conrad Borchers; Sebastian Simon; Elham Tajik; Amine Hatun Ataş; Berkan Celik; Francesco Balzan; Bahar Shahrokhian
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: OSF version 1 record; no archival venue verified in inspected sources
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official OSF full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: uses the human CSCL survey analysis by Simon et al. (2024 manuscript) as its benchmark; system paper is distinct but benchmark-dependent
evidence_records.Research objective: Test whether an orchestrated Claude multi-agent system can conduct an end-to-end inductive thematic analysis without human supervision while providing robustness, traceability and human-aligned themes.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: An orchestrator spawns translation, multiple coding, consensus, theme and reporting agents on 200 one-sentence survey responses; outputs are repeated 20 times and qualitatively compared by the original human coding team to its prior four-question analysis.
evidence_records.Domain: computer-supported collaborative learning definitions and future priorities
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 200 predominantly single-sentence responses; human benchmark contains 553 initial codes and four question-specific theme sets
evidence_records.Language: multilingual input including French, translated to English by an agent
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: no sensitive content identified; participant governance not described
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: one agentic process prompt describes thematic-analysis stages; orchestrator delegates translation, independent coding, consensus, themes and report assembly; temperature above zero for coding
evidence_records.Agent roles: orchestrator; translator; independent coding agents; consensus agent; independent theme agents; final report assembly
evidence_records.Human role: prior team of three coders plus fourth consensus researcher creates benchmark; the same team gives qualitative feedback on the system output; no humans supervise the automated run
evidence_records.Generated outputs: translations, codes linked to responses, consensus code sets, themes linked to codes and a final report
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: code-to-response and theme-to-code links plus intermediate outputs; example output and materials in GitHub
evidence_records.Baselines: manual inductive analysis by three coders plus a consensus researcher
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: 20 repeated system runs; no formal similarity definition, run parameters or seeds reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: no quantitative AI–human theme metric; human benchmark Krippendorff alpha .934 is reported from the source analysis
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: original human coding team reviews the multi-agent themes and comments on overlap and depth
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: three original independent coders and a fourth discrepancy resolver; expertise details not reported; external experts not used
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: human source analysis Krippendorff alpha .934; no reliability for the qualitative evaluation of system outputs
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: none for AI–human alignment; 'nearly matched' is a narrative judgment
evidence_records.Principal results: The authors report near alignment on three of four human themes per question and partial alignment on the fourth, semantic consistency across 20 runs, and less complexity/depth on ambiguous distinctions; no numerical theme-overlap result supports 'human-quality'.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: described as substantially reducing time/effort; no measured time or cost; authors expect nonlinear cost growth with longer inputs
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: discusses bias, socio-technical opacity and the need for human oversight; no study-specific consent/ethics statement
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: GitHub repository/output at https://github.com/se6astians1mon/TA-MAS and open dataset/coding results claimed
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: single-sentence corpus; ambiguous/contextual distinctions missed; long-context constraints; prompt robustness not tested; validity judgments made by the original team; external evaluation needed; costs may scale nonlinearly
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: The same benchmark team evaluates the output without blinding, alignment is not operationally defined, and the repeated-run 'semantic consistency' claim lacks a metric. Consensus among identical model instances does not represent independent interpretive plurality.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Automates and reuses the CSCL dataset and human coding reported in Simon et al.; draws on Barany, De Paoli, Tai and Yan workflows.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Raises multi-agent provenance and repeated-run evaluation in importance, but the ARR design should rank external blinded theme assessment and formal stability metrics above autonomous consensus.

evidence_records.Full citation: Osian, Sam, Arpan Dutta, Sahil Bhandari, Iain E. Buchan, and Dan W. Joyce. 2025. Automating Thematic Review of Prevention of Future Deaths Reports: Replicating the ONS Child Suicide Study Using Large Language Models. arXiv:2507.20786v1.
evidence_records.Title: Automating Thematic Review of Prevention of Future Deaths Reports: Replicating the ONS Child Suicide Study using Large Language Models
evidence_records.Authors: Sam Osian; Arpan Dutta; Sahil Bhandari; Iain E. Buchan; Dan W. Joyce
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v1 dated 28 July 2025; manuscript dated 29 July 2025
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: computational replication of the ONS 2025 child-suicide PFD bulletin; PFD Toolkit v0.3.3 application paper
evidence_records.Research objective: Determine whether an automated open-source pipeline can reproduce ONS child-suicide report identification and its fixed 23-subtheme review, with clinical screening validation and runtime measurement.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: PFD Toolkit scrapes/OCRs 4,249 reports, uses GPT-4.1 to screen child-suicide relevance and assign ONS-defined addressee categories and 23 fixed concern subthemes, then validates only the relevance screen on a 144-report stratified sample adjudicated by clinicians.
evidence_records.Domain: coronial Prevention of Future Deaths reports and child suicide
evidence_records.Dataset name: Courts and Tribunals Judiciary PFD archive, July 2013–November 2023; ONS child-suicide coding frame
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: public reports; sensitive content redacted by Chief Coroner
evidence_records.Number of participants: decedents in public reports; no research participants recruited
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 4,249 documents; 23 concern subthemes under six themes and five addressee categories
evidence_records.Document length: mixed long text, HTML, scanned PDF/images
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: public coronial records concerning deaths and suicide; official redactions applied
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-4.1 via cloud API; PFD Toolkit v0.3.3
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: user-defined structured Boolean extraction/coding prompts with Pydantic JSON validation; optional supporting-text evidence
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: single-model pipeline with OCR, scraping and schema stages
evidence_records.Agent roles: extract/OCR, screen relevance, assign fixed codes, tabulate; human review can audit evidence but was not part of production run
evidence_records.Human role: three blinded clinicians independently classify the 144-item screening sample and reach consensus; researchers compare aggregate ONS counts; no human validation of the 23 theme assignments
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: report for screening and report × category/subtheme for coding
evidence_records.Generated outputs: structured Boolean relevance, addressee and concern labels; aggregate tables; optional supporting passages
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: optional supporting text for every coded item; public source reports and open toolkit
evidence_records.Baselines: ONS aggregate count (37); post-consensus clinician screen labels; human pre-consensus reliability
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: one end-to-end run; no repeat/seed reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: raw agreement, Cohen kappa with 95% CI, Fleiss kappa, counts and wall-clock runtime
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: balanced/decoy-boosted sample of 72 pipeline-positive and 72 pipeline-negative reports, rated independently by three blinded clinicians and consensus-adjudicated
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: three Royal College of Psychiatrists clinicians with serious-incident and coronial-system experience
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: clinician Fleiss κ=.766 (95% CI .672–.861); pipeline versus consensus Cohen κ=.82 (95% CI .66–.98), raw agreement 91%
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: fixed-n binary kappa power calculation and confidence intervals
evidence_records.Principal results: The pipeline found 72 reports versus the ONS's 37 (62 within the ONS window). On the enriched screening sample it achieved κ=.82 and 91% agreement. It completed screening, fixed-frame coding and tabulation in 8m16s.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: 8 minutes 16 seconds on a consumer Ubuntu laptop plus GPT-4.1 cloud calls versus a manual process described as months; API cost not reported
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: University of Liverpool ethics approval ref. 16296 (4 June 2025); public, officially redacted reports; approval explicitly covered third-party API processing
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: PFD Toolkit and example notebooks at https://github.com/Sam-Osian/PFD-toolkit
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: ages sometimes absent; ONS report-level labels unavailable; report-level versus mention-level counting prevents direct theme-count comparison; model dependence; no direct report-by-report ONS comparison
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: The impressive κ validates only child-suicide screening on a prevalence-enriched sample, not the 23 concern codes. Calling aggregate fixed-frame tabulation a replicated thematic analysis overstates evidence, and ONS/toolkit counts differ in date coverage and counting unit.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Reimplements the ONS bulletin using the authors' PFD Toolkit; not independent of its public code frame or archive.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strong provenance, expert blinding and explicit runtime move evidence-linked fixed-frame projects upward, but ARR evaluation must separate screening from code/theme validity and evaluate each stage.

evidence_records.Full citation: Rizvi, Naba, Harper Strickland, Saleha Ahmedi, Aekta Kallepalli, Isha Khirwadkar, William Wu, Imani N. S. Munyaka, and Nedjma Ousidhoum. 2025. Beyond Keywords: Evaluating Large Language Model Classification of Nuanced Ableism. arXiv:2505.20500v1.
evidence_records.Title: Beyond Keywords: Evaluating Large Language Model Classification of Nuanced Ableism
evidence_records.Authors: Naba Rizvi; Harper Strickland; Saleha Ahmedi; Aekta Kallepalli; Isha Khirwadkar; William Wu; Imani N. S. Munyaka; Nedjma Ousidhoum
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: follow-on evaluation using the authors' AUTALIC dataset (Rizvi et al., arXiv:2410.16520)
evidence_records.Research objective: Evaluate how four open LLMs classify contextual anti-autistic ableism, whose human perspectives they reproduce, and whether personas/examples align them with autistic-community judgments.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: mixed quantitative classification plus qualitative comparison of human and LLM explanations
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Four local models classify 2,121 AUTALIC sentences under persona/in-context conditions; agreement is measured against community-informed labels, while six author-annotators manually analyze 100 generated rationales against 52 human justifications.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: deductive classification plus inductive/manual error analysis
evidence_records.Domain: anti-autistic ableism in contextual online speech
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: publicly described dataset; availability location not stated in the inspected paper
evidence_records.Number of documents: 2,121 core sentences; 284 disjoint in-context examples; 283 consensus ground-truth subset; 100-rationale qualitative sample
evidence_records.Number of participants: AUTALIC annotators plus two autistic graduate validators and six author error analysts; total original annotator count not stated here
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 2,121 contextual sentences; each original annotator classified 1,121; 52 human justifications
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: ableist/hate speech with slurs and violence references; trigger warning supplied
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Gemma-2 9B; Mistral 7B; Llama-3 8B; DeepSeek-LLM 7B, via Ollama defaults
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: binary/ternary labels plus under-five-word rationale; shuffled repeat; personas and 284 disjoint in-context examples stratified by autism/bias measures
evidence_records.Agent roles: classify contextual speech and generate short justification
evidence_records.Human role: community annotators create labels; two autistic graduate students validate a consensus subset; six author-annotators conduct independent qualitative error analysis and discussion
evidence_records.Generated outputs: ableist/not/uncertain labels, psychometric-test responses and brief rationales
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: rationales remain tied to source sentences and are compared with human justifications; paper prints error examples
evidence_records.Baselines: human perspective strata; binary versus ternary schemes; base, persona and in-context prompts; four models
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: sentences reshuffled for a second scheme/self-consistency comparison; default Ollama sampling, seeds not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: Fleiss kappa, label-frequency sensitivity/confidence z-scores and psychometric-scale scores
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: two autistic validators retain only unanimous labels for 283 sentences; six authors independently inspect 100 model outputs for contextual/reasoning errors
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two autistic graduate students; six author-annotators; wider AUTALIC annotators characterized by AQ, SATA and IAT
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: only full-agreement items retained for the 283-item reference; numerical kappa values are presented graphically rather than recoverable from text
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: Fleiss kappa and normalized/z-scored psychometric comparisons; manual pattern analysis
evidence_records.Principal results: Models reproduced biased perspectives better than autistic/accepting perspectives, remained keyword-driven despite examples/personas, and were up to four times more likely than humans to flag some speech. Twenty percent of the 100 error-analysis items changed labels/reasons across runs; binary labels improved self-agreement but not contextual validity.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: university IRB approval; volunteers received trigger warnings and could withdraw; limitations of medical-model instruments and Western/English sampling are discussed
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: AUTALIC is cited as a public dataset/preprint; models are open and locally run, but code/prompt repository not stated in inspected text
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: four small models; psychometric instruments have limitations and were administered once; mostly Western computing students; no multilingual/cross-cultural generalization
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Reference construction excludes disagreement, which can inflate apparent certainty; using Fleiss kappa for model-to-human comparisons is not fully specified; community plurality is partly reduced to binary ground truth.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Directly reuses and extends AUTALIC annotations with model rationales, personas and community-sensitive error analysis.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Materially elevates plurality- and subgroup-sensitive evaluation: rationales must be checked by affected communities, and aggregate agreement cannot substitute for context, speaker identity and impact.

evidence_records.Full citation: Ghali, Mohammed-Khalil, Abdelrahman Farrag, Sarah Lam, and Daehan Won. 2025. BEYONDWORDS Is All You Need: Agentic Generative AI Based Social Media Themes Extractor. arXiv:2503.01880v1.
evidence_records.Title: BEYONDWORDS is All You Need: Agentic Generative AI based Social Media Themes Extractor
evidence_records.Authors: Mohammed-Khalil Ghali; Abdelrahman Farrag; Sarah Lam; Daehan Won
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v1 dated 26 February 2025; manuscript says preprint submitted 5 March 2025
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: standalone BEYONDWORDS system; dataset is a filtered reuse of a prior #ActuallyAutistic Twitter corpus
evidence_records.Research objective: Propose a scalable pipeline combining embeddings, compression, SVD/k-means and a two-LLM feedback loop to label themes in autistic-community tweets.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Embeddings of roughly 200,000 filtered tweets are autoencoder-compressed, reduced by SVD and k-means clustered into k=3; 68 high-silhouette tweets per cluster are passed to GPT-4o mini to name themes, and a second instance of the same model scores/refines them.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: nominally inductive, operationally unsupervised clustering plus LLM cluster labeling
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: prior scraped social-media dataset; release/access not stated
evidence_records.Number of documents: approximately 200,000 filtered tweets from an original 3.1 million
evidence_records.Number of participants: 17,323 unique accounts in the source corpus; identity claims inferred from profiles/hashtags
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: ~200,000 English #ActuallyAutistic tweets; 68 selected exemplars per each of three clusters
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: public social-media data from a marginalized health/disability community; no governance or consent discussion
evidence_records.Exact model/version: all-MiniLM-L6-v2; bge-base-en-v1.5; bge-m3; GPT-4o mini for both extractor and evaluator
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: structured chain-of-thought keyword/group/theme stages; second same-model agent assigns an unspecified quality score and feedback until an unspecified threshold/iteration limit
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: autoencoders trained at 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 compression; no LLM fine-tuning
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: two LLM-role instances after embedding/clustering pipeline
evidence_records.Agent roles: LLM1 extracts keywords/groups/themes; LLM2 grades and critiques; LLM1 revises
evidence_records.Human role: no human analyst, code validator or community reviewer reported
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: tweet embedding/cluster and sampled cluster exemplars
evidence_records.Generated outputs: three clusters, keywords, theme labels/descriptions, word clouds and Sankey diagrams
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: themes are associated with sampled cluster keywords; no code-to-document audit trail, exemplar table or human verification
evidence_records.Baselines: embedding sizes and compression versus no compression; no human thematic baseline
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: not reported; k-means/random/LLM seeds and number of feedback iterations not stated
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: autoencoder validation loss, explained variance, Calinski–Harabasz, Davies–Bouldin and silhouette indices
evidence_records.Principal results: The pipeline fixes three clusters and names them content quality/engagement, autistic rights/acceptance, and mental health/well-being. Large embeddings with compression show silhouette .48 versus .04 without, but no evidence evaluates the qualitative meaning, inclusiveness or factual grounding of these themes.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: scalability/cost-effectiveness asserted; no time, token or cost measurements
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: no study-specific ethics, consent, privacy or community-governance statement identified
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: no code, prompts, model snapshots, data release or run configuration identified
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: multistep complexity; dependence on embedding quality; bias; SVD/k-means parameter sensitivity; real-time processing and user feedback left for future work
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Cochran's survey-proportion formula does not establish semantic representativeness of top-silhouette cluster exemplars. Both LLM roles use the same model, thresholds are unstated, and internal clustering scores cannot validate themes or claims about autistic people's priorities.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Reuses an earlier 3.1M-tweet dataset; no independent human thematic comparator.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: A strong negative design case: clustering metrics and self-critique should not qualify as thematic validity; ARR should require document-level provenance, affected-community review and repeat/prompt sensitivity.

evidence_records.Full citation: De Paoli, Stefano. 2025. Can Machines Perform a Qualitative Data Analysis? Reading the Debate with Alan Turing. arXiv:2512.04121v1.
evidence_records.Title: Can machines perform a qualitative data analysis? Reading the debate with Alan Turing
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v1; empirical run reports Azure GPT-4o used in December 2025

evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: author's iterative thematic-analysis program; reuses Dunn et al. 2020 data and directly rebuts Jowsey et al. 2025's Copilot reanalysis
evidence_records.Research objective: Reframe the LLM/qualitative-analysis debate as empirical evaluation of a human–machine system and show how staged prompting changes results on one dataset previously used to argue failure.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: inductive thematic reanalysis plus critical/philosophical essay
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: One researcher reanalyzes 33 archived interviews with Azure GPT-4o: document-wise zero-shot codes, pairwise code deduplication with retained quotes/merge reasons, and one or more theme-grouping prompts, then narratively compares counts, coverage and quote fidelity with Dunn and Jowsey outputs.

evidence_records.Dataset name: Dunn et al. 2020 UK Data Archive dataset
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: archived open-access/controlled data; author obtained archive permission for Azure processing
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 146 parent codes reduced to 52; 115 practitioner codes reduced to 49; themes also generated for combined data
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: mental-health and family interviews; archive permission obtained for cloud analysis
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-4o via Azure, used December 2025; exact snapshot not stated
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: one interview at a time with iteratively designed zero-shot coding prompt; hierarchical pairwise duplicate merging; theme grouping at temperature .1; coding temperature/top_p 0; prompts appended
evidence_records.Agent roles: model produces codes/quotes, merges duplicates and groups codes into themes; researcher designs, stages, inspects and reruns the process
evidence_records.Human role: sole author selects the design, counts participants, sets prompts/parameters, interprets comparisons and argues validity; original Dunn researchers provide the published human comparator but do not evaluate new output
evidence_records.Generated outputs: codes with verbatim quotes, pairwise merge decisions/descriptions and parent/practitioner/combined themes
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: codes preserve associated source quotations; merge reasons and full coding trees are retained; appended prompts and cited open-source code
evidence_records.Baselines: Jowsey et al.'s one-shot Copilot output and Dunn et al.'s published human analysis
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: prompt developed over several experiments and themes may be regenerated; exact run count/seed not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: descriptive counts and saturation ratios; no formal semantic/alignment metric
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: author-led narrative comparison of theme breadth, group coverage and quote traceability; no blinded or independent evaluation
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: one author/researcher for the new analysis; original human analysis had two researchers and participant discussion
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: not reported for the new analysis
evidence_records.Principal results: Staged processing produced codes and themes for parents, practitioners and combined data, retained traceable quotations, and avoided the fabricated-quote/omitted-group failures reported for Copilot. The author explicitly does not claim the machine analysis is better than Dunn's or establish a universal positive answer.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: permission from the UK Data Archive for Azure analysis; no new participant consent/ethics detail reported
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: prompts in appendix; cited open-source pairwise-comparison code (De Paoli and Fawzi 2025); underlying archive data
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: one compact dataset is used to challenge a prior design; no claim that the artificial analysis surpasses the original human study; results depend on the hybrid design and iterative choices
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: The paper is a polemical single-author rebuttal with no blind independent assessment; better process/output than one weak Copilot setup does not establish qualitative validity or equivalence to human interpretation.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Extends De Paoli 2024 and pairwise-saturation work; directly depends on Dunn 2020 and Jowsey 2025 for data/comparators.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strengthens staged document-wise provenance and the need to evaluate systems rather than model metaphysics, while reinforcing that the ARR project needs independent judges and predefined 'good enough' criteria.

evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: qualitative case study using inductive thematic analysis and COREQ
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Researchers purposefully retrieve 3,120 comments/replies, retain/code 1,566 using NVivo and unnamed generative-AI theme suggestions, independently validate/refine preliminary codes, then one lead author codes the remaining corpus with team consultation and reports frequencies/quotes.

evidence_records.Authors: Sky Wei Chee Koh; Eunice Rui Ning Wong; John Chong Min Tan; Stephanie C. C. van der Lubbe; Jun Cong Goh; Ethan Sheng Yong Ching; Ian Wen Yih Chia; Si Hui Low; Ping Young Ang; Queenie Quek; Mehul Motani; Jose M. Valderas
evidence_records.Venue: Journal of Medical Internet Research 27: e74231
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; publisher/PMC full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: standalone HCAT(GP) validation/application; manually coded corpus supplies the reference
evidence_records.Research objective: Evaluate three off-the-shelf LLMs against trained human HCAT(GP) classifications and use Claude to generate a 15-topic complaint taxonomy.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: AI complaint categorization and thematic analysis
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Four trained humans double-code 1,816 complaints under fixed HCAT(GP) fields; three LLMs independently reproduce those fields with structured prompts, while Claude separately assigns a generated 15-category topic scheme that receives no human-validity evaluation.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: deductive HCAT classification plus model-generated topical taxonomy
evidence_records.Domain: patient complaints in Singapore public primary care
evidence_records.Dataset name: unified feedback management system, seven clinics, 2021
evidence_records.Number of participants: 1,816 complaints, mostly from patients/family; unique complainant count not reported
evidence_records.Language: translated to English when needed using Microsoft Translator; includes Singapore English
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: de-identified patient complaints; restricted for privacy and institutional reputation
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-3.5-turbo; GPT-4o mini; Claude 3.5 Sonnet; exact snapshots not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: single-complaint structured JSON prompts with verbatim HCAT definitions/keywords; summary then classification ('chain-of-thought'); ground-truth category is supplied when predicting severity
evidence_records.Agent roles: summarize complaint, assign fixed HCAT fields; Claude also creates/assigns a 15-topic taxonomy
evidence_records.Human role: four trained coders double-code every complaint; third coder and consensus resolve disagreements; researchers design prompts and compare models
evidence_records.Generated outputs: summaries, HCAT classifications and one of 15 generated complaint themes
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: complaint-level JSON output; prompt/code notebook in supplement; raw complaints restricted
evidence_records.Baselines: double-coded HCAT labels; GPT-3.5 predecessor versus GPT-4o mini and Claude
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: one classification per model/complaint; no repeat or seed reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: accuracy, precision/recall/F1, concordance, Cohen kappa and paired McNemar tests
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: all complaints independently assigned to two trained coders with third-coder/consensus resolution
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: four HCAT-trained coders: two physicians and two medical students
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: pre-consensus human reliability not reported; model–human κ ranges .114–.623 by field
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive statistics, fieldwise accuracy/F1/concordance/kappa and McNemar comparisons
evidence_records.Principal results: Average concordance was 61.9% for GPT-3.5, 68.7% GPT-4o mini and 68.8% Claude. Domain κ was about .61–.62, category .52–.57, stage .47–.56, but severity/harm κ only .114–.239 despite higher raw accuracy. Claude's 15 themes were reported only as frequencies.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: NHG Domain-Specific Review Board 2022/00333; waiver of consent; de-identification; restricted data
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Multimedia Appendix 1 contains prompts and Jupyter Notebook code; data are not public
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: 2.6% truncation; one-label ground truth oversimplifies multi-issue complaints; human subjectivity; 2021/COVID context; class imbalance; pretrained models and undisclosed training/model details; language variation; no conventional ML/BERT comparator
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Supplying true category when predicting severity leaks ground-truth information into that field. The 15-topic 'thematic analysis' has no human comparison or grounding evaluation, and fieldwise raw accuracy is misleading under imbalance, as the low harm/severity kappas show.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: uses established HCAT(GP) taxonomy and its human training; distinct from earlier Lee et al. ChatGPT complaint/thematic work
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strongly supports multi-field, chance-corrected reporting and expert double coding; also shows ARR must prohibit label leakage and separately validate generated themes rather than borrowing credibility from fixed-field results.

quality_scores.Title: Automated Quality Assessment for LLM-Based Complex Qualitative Coding: A Confidence-Diversity Framework

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: Five LLMs independently perform three pre-labelled supervised classification benchmarks; confidence and vote entropy are correlated with benchmark correctness, optimized into a weighted score, transferred among domains, and used in a simulated three-tier verification policy.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Adequate for the stated claim: 2017 Supreme Court term benchmark; SemEval-2019 Task 4 hyperpartisan news; MTSamples

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Adequate for the stated claim: task-specific zero/few-context classification prompts plus a risk-framed self-assessment from 0.50–0.99; exact prompts are in the replication package

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: confidence-only, entropy-only, equal weighting, domain-optimized and global weights; cross-domain weight transfer

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Absent or inadequate: none; triage verification is simulated rather than conducted

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: accuracy, Pearson correlation, bootstrap confidence intervals, Bonferroni-adjusted p-values, effect sizes and verification-effort simulations

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Absent or inadequate: The paper calls fixed benchmark prediction 'qualitative coding'; its quality signal is validated against known labels despite motivating deployment without ground truth. Weight optimization and triage appear evaluated on the same three datasets, and '100% transfer success' means improvement over a weak confidence-only baseline, not preservation of qualitative validity.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: case-level model outputs and benchmark labels are retained in the replication data; no interpretive quotation trail is evaluated

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: one prediction per model/case; 1,000 bootstrap resamples; model sampling seed not reported

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: secondary analysis of public/de-identified benchmarks; authors state no new ethics approval was required

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Adequate for the stated claim: Harvard Dataverse draft replication package DOI 10.7910/DVN/GM8T8Q with datasets, code, optimization and triage scripts

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: The paper calls fixed benchmark prediction 'qualitative coding'; its quality signal is validated against known labels despite motivating deployment without ground truth. Weight optimization and triage appear evaluated on the same three datasets, and '100% transfer success' means improvement over a weak confidence-only baseline, not preservation of qualitative validity.

quality_scores.Title: BEYONDWORDS is All You Need: Agentic Generative AI based Social Media Themes Extractor

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Absent or inadequate: Embeddings of roughly 200,000 filtered tweets are autoencoder-compressed, reduced by SVD and k-means clustered into k=3; 68 high-silhouette tweets per cluster are passed to GPT-4o mini to name themes, and a second instance of the same model scores/refines them.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: structured chain-of-thought keyword/group/theme stages; second same-model agent assigns an unspecified quality score and feedback until an unspecified threshold/iteration limit

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Absent or inadequate: embedding sizes and compression versus no compression; no human thematic baseline

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Absent or inadequate: autoencoder validation loss, explained variance, Calinski–Harabasz, Davies–Bouldin and silhouette indices

quality_scores.Title: Classifying Patient Complaints Using Artificial Intelligence-Powered Large Language Models: Cross-Sectional Study

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: Four trained humans double-code 1,816 complaints under fixed HCAT(GP) fields; three LLMs independently reproduce those fields with structured prompts, while Claude separately assigns a generated 15-category topic scheme that receives no human-validity evaluation.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Adequate for the stated claim: unified feedback management system, seven clinics, 2021

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Adequate for the stated claim: single-complaint structured JSON prompts with verbatim HCAT definitions/keywords; summary then classification ('chain-of-thought'); ground-truth category is supplied when predicting severity

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Adequate for the stated claim: double-coded HCAT labels; GPT-3.5 predecessor versus GPT-4o mini and Claude

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Adequate for the stated claim: all complaints independently assigned to two trained coders with third-coder/consensus resolution

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Adequate for the stated claim: accuracy, precision/recall/F1, concordance, Cohen kappa and paired McNemar tests

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Partial or claim-limited: Supplying true category when predicting severity leaks ground-truth information into that field. The 15-topic 'thematic analysis' has no human comparison or grounding evaluation, and fieldwise raw accuracy is misleading under imbalance, as the low harm/severity kappas show.
